audit.whatIsWrong: Sky Splitter is called a stun in three places: wants.foe[0] 'Land his Sky Splitter stun to lock you out of your W-taunt channel', spikes[3] 'his W-heal brawl and Sky Splitter stun out-stat your plateaued tankiness', whys[6] 'his W-heal and Sky Splitter stun out-scale my plateaued tankiness'.
audit.why: Sky Splitter slows — it has no stun on it at all. The stun in Volibear's kit is Thundering Smash (Q), which speeds him toward you and stuns the first enemy he then attacks. Getting this wrong inverts the entire defensive plan: the page tells you to fear a 1200-range ranged ability that cannot stop your W channel, and to relax about the 300-range approach that can.
audit.corrected: Sky Splitter is a 1200-range slow that also shields Volibear if he stands in his own blast. The stun is Thundering Smash — he speeds at you and the stun lands on his next attack, so the tell is the approach, not the lightning.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (E Sky Splitter: 'dealing damage and Slowing enemies while granting Volibear a Shield if he's inside the blast radius', flags projectile,slow,shield,zone; Q Thundering Smash: 'gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks', flags hardCC,autoReset)

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Neither layer carries a single number, and breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5] all just say 'bait Thundering Smash'.
audit.why: The numbers make this lane legible. Thundering Smash is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 — a real window. Frenzied Maul is a flat 5 seconds, which is why extended trades lose: you cannot outlast a heal that comes back every five seconds. Sky Splitter is a flat 16 and Stormbringer is 160/135/110. 'Short trades, never long ones' becomes a rule you can time instead of a slogan.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash 12s at rank 1; Frenzied Maul a flat 5s; Sky Splitter a flat 16s; Stormbringer 160s at rank 1. Commit in the 12 seconds after his Q, and get out before the second Maul.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says Sky Splitter reaches 1200 units, or that it shields him.
audit.why: 1200 outranges Winds of War's 825 by a wide margin, so the entry's plan of 'poke and clear from max Q range' is not actually safe — he can chip you from outside your poke and take no risk. And the shield only applies if Volibear stands in his own blast, which is a visible tell that he intends to walk in rather than poke.
audit.corrected: Sky Splitter is 1200 range against your 825, so he out-pokes you; but it only shields him if he stands in the blast — that is his commit tell.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (E range 1200, shield conditional on being inside the blast radius)

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why says 'the dash is interruptible and root-able mid-flight', and spikes[0]/early describe Thundering Smash as a 'Q-empowered dash'.
audit.why: Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel. Volibear has no root and Thundering Smash is not a dash — it is a movement-speed buff toward enemies whose stun lands on his next attack. Calling it a dash makes players wait for a leap that never comes; the real cue is him walking at you faster than usual.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash is a speed-up, not a dash, and the stun only lands on the attack that follows. Justice Punch cannot be interrupted once travelling, and Volibear has no root.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (Q: 'gains speed towards enemies, Stunning and damaging the first one he Attacks')
wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel)

audit.whatIsWrong: Frenzied Maul is described only as a heal. It is never identified as an on-hit application, and Thundering Smash is never identified as an auto reset.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags all three for this pairing: needs-antiheal (Frenzied Maul), onhit-itemization (Frenzied Maul) and autoreset-burst-tell (Thundering Smash). The kit confirms the onHit and autoReset flags. Practically: his damage rides on attack speed stacked by The Relentless Storm, so armour alone reads the trade wrong, and his opener is auto-into-instant-Q rather than two separate actions.
audit.corrected: Frenzied Maul applies on-hit and his attack speed ramps with The Relentless Storm, so armour alone misreads the trade — health and Grievous Wounds do more. Thundering Smash resets his auto, so the stun and the hit arrive together.
sources: champ-data/_kits/volibear.json (W flags heal,onHit, cooldown 5; Q flags hardCC,autoReset; P The Relentless Storm grants attack speed)

audit.whatIsWrong: The stage chart reads Skill, Volibear, Volibear, Volibear, Volibear, Volibear, Skill — five rows to Volibear in a 50.0% matchup — while the prose gives Level 3 and Level 6 to Galio outright ('At 3 my Shield-of-Durand taunt into E-knockup punishes his Q-dash step-up', 'Hero's Entrance is my biggest spike') and calls Levels 2, 4-5 and first item even.
audit.why: Five of seven rows to one side in a coin-flip lane is not a reading of the matchup, it is a template. The prose already contains a per-row verdict; the chart just does not match it.
audit.corrected: Volibear, Skill, Galio, Skill, Galio, Skill, Volibear.
sources: scratchpad packet galio.json entry volibear (50.0%, 18 games)

Level 6 is my real spike, and it's not the 1v1: Hero's Entrance means even if he's edging me top, I shield a fight and drop a knockup-taunt onto mid or bot. His stun is Thundering Smash on a 12-second cooldown, not the lightning, so count that and commit after it. Level 6 is your real spike and it is not the 1v1: Hero's Entrance drops a knockup-taunt onto mid or bot. Watch Stormbringer — it disables your turret before a dive.

edits.before: This trends back to him past two items. Shield of Durand's damage reduction is heavily tilted toward magic, so it does little against a tanky AD brawler, and his W-bite heal plus Sky Splitter stun out-stat me once my tankiness and damage plateau while he keeps scaling and diving. My job here isn't to win the splitpush 1v1 — I won't. It's to use Hero's Entrance presence to make picks and start fights elsewhere, taunting his bruiser off my carries while my team trades the side lane.
